To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
women’s dehumanization of female competitors is enhanced by their hormonal shift across menstrual cycles and that it is associated with women’s intra-sexual competition.

1) normally ovulating women, but not women who use hormonal contraceptive, dehumanize other woman more during the high conception risk phase of menstrual cycle; 2) normally ovulating woman, but not woman who use hormonal contraceptive show increased intra-sexual competition during the high conception phase of the menstrual cycle; and 3) dehumanization of woman and intra-sexual competition are positively correlated only for normally ovulating women.

(1) normally ovulating women dehumanize other female targets more than men and elderly people; (2) normally ovulating woman’s level of dehumanizing other women increases when the risk of conceiving with a man is higher; (3) hormonal contraceptives reduce the level of de-humanization; and (4) dehumanization is positively correlated with intra-sexual mate-competition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the menstrual cycle in the emergence of dehumanization and intra-sexual competition among women, and it is the first to investigate this issue.
understanding the role of menstrual cycle–related hormonal shift in female dehumanizing behavior and its relation with intra-sexual competitiveness.
the psychological mechanisms underlying dehumanization and the role of the hormonal cycle in the emergence of this phenomenon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dehumanization is elicited by hormonal shift and associated with women's mate-attraction goal.
the dehumanization of the female other is a consequence of the menstrual cycle and it is associated with the intra-sexual competition of women.
dehumanization is not only a male behavior, but it is a female behavior as well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
women who are not using hormonal contraceptives show a pattern of increased dehumanization of female targets and increased sexual competition as they approach ovulation.
women’s dehumanization of their female peers increases as the likelihood of conception is enhanced, and this is linked to their mate-attraction strategies.
women’s mate attraction goals can be associated with dehumanizing other women.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the menstrual cycle is a key factor to take into account in the study of women’s inter-sexual and intra-sexual behaviors.
the menstrual cycle is an overlooked factor that may contribute to the perpetuation of sexism.
the menstrual cycle can influence how women perceive other women.
